stories.headline: Pentagon Signs Deals With 7 AI Companies for Classified Military Networks; Anthropic Excluded

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon reached agreements with SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services to deploy frontier AI on classified networks for lawful operational use.
key_facts.excerpt: The War Department has entered into agreements with seven of the world's leading frontier artificial intelligence companies, SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services to deploy their advanced AI capabilities on the Department's classified networks for lawful operational use.

key_facts.fact: The AI tools will be integrated into Impact Level 6 (IL6) and Impact Level 7 (IL7) classified network environments, the Pentagon's highest security tiers.
key_facts.excerpt: Integrating secure frontier AI capabilities into the Department's Impact Level 6 (IL6) and Impact Level 7 (IL7) network environments will streamline data synthesis, elevate situational understanding, and augment warfighter decision-making in complex operational environments.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon's GenAI.mil platform already has over 1.3 million users who have generated tens of millions of prompts and deployed hundreds of thousands of agents in five months.
key_facts.excerpt: Over 1.3 million Department personnel have used the platform, generating tens of millions of prompts and deploying hundreds of thousands of agents in only five months.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic was excluded from the agreements after the Pentagon labeled it a supply-chain risk last month over a dispute about guardrails for military use of its AI tools.
key_facts.excerpt: Another AI giant Anthropic has been in dispute with the Pentagon over guardrails for how the military could use its artificial intelligence tools, which led the Pentagon to label Anthropic a supply-chain risk last month, barring its use by the Pentagon and its contractors.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon described the agreements as accelerating its transformation toward becoming an 'AI-first fighting force' to maintain decision superiority across all warfare domains.
key_facts.excerpt: These agreements accelerate the transformation toward establishing the United States military as an AI-first fighting force and will strengthen our warfighters' ability to maintain decision superiority across all domains of warfare.

key_facts.fact: Oracle also joined the roster of companies later on Friday, bringing the total to eight firms deploying AI on classified networks.
key_facts.excerpt: On Friday, the Pentagon posted on the social media site X that Oracle Corp. had also joined the roster of technology companies that had agreed to deploy their AI tools on classified networks.

sources.title: Pentagon reaches agreements with leading AI companies
Pentagon Reaches Agreements With Top AI Companies, but Not Anthropic

stories.headline: Huawei Expects AI Chip Revenue to Hit ~$12B in 2026, Up 60%+ as DeepSeek Drives Demand

key_facts.fact: Huawei expects AI chip revenue to reach about $12 billion in 2026 based on orders already received, up from $7.5 billion in 2025 — a jump of at least 60%.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chinese tech company expects revenue from its chips to reach about $12 billion this year based on orders it has already received, up from $7.5 billion in 2025.

key_facts.fact: The majority of 2026 orders are for Huawei's latest Ascend 950PR processor, which entered mass production in March 2026, with an upgraded 950DT variant planned for Q4.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei received majority of orders this year for its latest Ascend processor 950PR, which entered mass production in March, and the firm plans to launch an upgraded version of 950DT in the fourth quarter.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's April 24 release of its V4 AI model, optimized for Huawei Ascend chips, triggered a wave of procurement from Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent.
key_facts.excerpt: The revenue surge has been supercharged by DeepSeek's release of its V4 AI model on April 24, which was specifically optimised to run on Huawei's Ascend chips. The move triggered a wave of procurement activity across China's largest technology companies, with Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent among those racing to secure supply.

key_facts.fact: Huawei plans to ship approximately 750,000 Ascend 950PR units in 2026, with full-scale shipments ramping in the second half.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei plans to ship approximately 750,000 units in 2026, with full-scale shipments ramping in the second half of the year.

key_facts.fact: TrendForce forecasts the Chinese high-end AI chip market will grow by more than 60% in 2026, with domestic chips potentially capturing about half the market.
key_facts.excerpt: Analysts at TrendForce forecast the Chinese high-end AI chip market will grow by more than 60% in 2026, with domestically produced chips potentially capturing around half of that market.

key_facts.fact: Morgan Stanley estimates the domestic Chinese AI chip supply at about $21 billion in 2026, with Huawei's projected $12 billion representing the single largest share.
key_facts.excerpt: This year, Morgan Stanley estimates the domestic Chinese AI chip supply at approximately $21 billion — with Huawei's projected $12 billion representing the single largest share.

stories.headline: Russia Now Imports Over 90% of Sanctioned Tech Through China, Up From 80% Last Year

key_facts.fact: Russia now imports more than 90% of its sanctioned technology through China, up from about 80% last year, according to people familiar with internal assessments.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia imports over 90% of sanctioned technologies through China, indicating Moscow's growing dependence on Beijing amid dictator Vladimir Putin's protracted war against Ukraine. This figure has risen from approximately 80% last year.

key_facts.fact: The sanctioned goods include semiconductors, integrated circuits, electronics, and machinery needed to produce weapons including missiles and drones.
key_facts.excerpt: The EU applies sanctions to deprive Russia of access to technologies needed to use or produce such weapons, including semiconductors, integrated circuits, electronics, and machinery.

key_facts.fact: Beyond components, China also provides Russia with geospatial intelligence, satellite imagery for military purposes, and drones, while restricting similar supplies to Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: In addition to technical components, China provides Russia with geospatial intelligence, satellite imagery for military purposes, and drones, while restricting similar supplies to Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: EU sanctions against Chinese and Hong Kong companies accused of helping Russia circumvent restrictions have not had the expected effect, and most EU countries are not ready for tougher measures against China.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the obvious support for the Russian military-industrial complex, most EU countries are currently avoiding the imposition of tough sanctions directly against China. EU leaders fear economic retaliation from Beijing.

key_facts.fact: According to Ukrainian intelligence, Russia has spent approximately $130 billion over the past four years to circumvent Western sanctions and purchase banned goods.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Ukrainian intelligence, Russia has spent approximately $130 billion over the past four years to circumvent Western sanctions and purchase banned goods.

stories.headline: Russia's New Soyuz-5 Rocket Aces Maiden Launch From Baikonur in First Debut in Decades

key_facts.fact: Russia's Soyuz-5 rocket lifted off for its first-ever flight on April 30 at 2:00 PM EDT from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on a successful suborbital test.
key_facts.excerpt: The Soyuz 5 lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (April 30), rising off a pad at the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan at 2:00 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT).

key_facts.fact: Roscosmos confirmed both first and second stages performed as planned, with a mockup payload launched onto the calculated suborbital trajectory before reentering over the Pacific Ocean.
key_facts.excerpt: The first and second stages of Soyuz 5 performed as planned, and a mockup was launched onto the calculated suborbital trajectory, followed by a reentry into an area in the Pacific Ocean previously closed to shipping and aviation.

key_facts.fact: Soyuz-5 was designed to replace Ukraine-built Zenit rockets — a critical need after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, severing access to Ukrainian rocketry expertise.
key_facts.excerpt: It 'was designed to replace the medium-class Zenit vehicles built in Ukraine and provide Russia with a first-stage booster for a future super-heavy rocket.'

key_facts.fact: The Soyuz-5 can haul about 20 tons to low Earth orbit, comparable to SpaceX's Falcon 9 (25.1 tons), but is fully expendable with no reusable first stage.
key_facts.excerpt: The rocket is comparable in size and lifting power to SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9; the Soyuz 5 can haul about 20 tons (18 metric tons) to low Earth orbit, compared to 25.1 tons (22.8 metric tons) for the SpaceX launcher. But the Falcon 9's first stage is reusable, whereas the Soyuz 5 is a completely expendable vehicle.

key_facts.fact: The rocket has been in development since 2017 and launched from Site 45/1 at Baikonur, which was originally built for Zenit launches.
key_facts.excerpt: It was from Site 45/1 that Soyuz-5 made its maiden flight. This was originally one of two Zenit launch pads at Baikonur.

sources.title: Russia's new homegrown Soyuz 5 rocket aces debut launch

stories.headline: Intellia's CRISPR Gene-Editing Therapy Hits Phase 3 Win With 87% Attack Reduction, Begins FDA Filing

key_facts.fact: Intellia Therapeutics reported positive Phase 3 HAELO trial results for lonvo-z, the world's first in vivo CRISPR-based gene-editing candidate to produce Phase 3 data.
key_facts.excerpt: Chief Executive Officer John Leonard described the update as a milestone for 'the entire CRISPR field' and people living with HAE, emphasizing Intellia's focus on in vivo gene editing delivered to the liver.

key_facts.fact: The primary endpoint was met with an 87% reduction in monthly attack rate (0.26 vs 2.1 for placebo) in patients with hereditary angioedema receiving a single dose of lonvo-z.
key_facts.excerpt: For the primary endpoint (weeks 5–28), the placebo arm had a mean of 2.1 attacks per month versus 0.26 for lonvo-z, an 87% reduction.

key_facts.fact: 62% of lonvo-z patients were completely attack-free and therapy-free during the evaluation period, compared to 11% on placebo; 100% of lonvo-z patients achieved some attack-rate reduction.
key_facts.excerpt: 62% of lonvo-z patients were attack-free during the efficacy observation period versus 11% on placebo. He emphasized that these patients were also 'therapy-free'... 100% of patients achieved an attack-rate reduction from baseline.

key_facts.fact: The trial enrolled 80 patients with Type 1 and Type 2 HAE, randomized 2:1 to a one-time 50 mg dose of lonvo-z or placebo, with all adverse events mild or moderate.
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 80 patients enrolled, with 52 assigned to lonvo-z and 28 to placebo... lonvo-z had a favorable safety and tolerability profile... with all events mild or moderate and no serious events in the lonvo-z arm.

key_facts.fact: Intellia initiated a rolling BLA filing with the FDA and aims for a commercial launch in the first half of 2027 if approved.
key_facts.excerpt: Leonard said Intellia recently initiated a rolling biologics license application (BLA) with the FDA... and aims, 'if approved,' to target a commercial launch in the first half of 2027.

key_facts.fact: U.S. spending on chronic HAE medications is about $4 billion annually, with about 7,000 treated patients in the U.S. and more than 60% on long-term prophylaxis.
key_facts.excerpt: He estimated there are about 7,000 treated HAE patients in the U.S., with more than 60% on LTP, and said U.S. spending is 'about $4 billion annually on chronic HAE medications alone.'

sources.title: Intellia Therapeutics Posts Phase 3 HAELO Win for lonvo-z, Begins Rolling FDA BLA Filing

stories.headline: FDA Approves First Non-Antipsychotic Drug for Alzheimer's Agitation, Affecting 76% of Patients

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Auvelity (dextromethorphan + bupropion) by Axsome Therapeutics for treating agitation in Alzheimer's dementia — the first non-antipsychotic approved for this condition.
key_facts.excerpt: AUVELITY is a first-in-class treatment for Alzheimer's disease agitation which targets the N-methyl D-aspartate (NMDA) and sigma-1 receptors.

key_facts.fact: Up to 76% of Alzheimer's patients experience agitation — including pacing, restlessness, and verbal or physical aggression — making it one of the most costly aspects of care.
key_facts.excerpt: Up to 76% of patients with Alzheimer's disease experience agitation.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 ADVANCE-1 trial, Auvelity showed statistically significant improvement in agitation symptoms at Week 5 vs placebo, with only 1.3% discontinuation due to adverse events (same as placebo).
key_facts.excerpt: ADVANCE-1... AUVELITY was statistically significantly superior to placebo in improvement of agitation symptoms as measured by the Cohen-Mansfield Agitation Inventory (CMAI) total score at Week 5... 1.3% of patients discontinued AUVELITY due to an adverse event, the same rate as placebo.

key_facts.fact: In the ACCORD-2 long-term study, patients continuing Auvelity experienced significantly longer time to relapse of agitation symptoms over 6 months vs those switched to placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: In ACCORD-2, the patients who continued treatment with AUVELITY experienced a statistically significantly longer time to relapse of agitation symptoms, measured by the CMAI, than did patients who switched to placebo.

key_facts.fact: Auvelity received both FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation and Priority Review for this indication; Alzheimer's disease affects more than 7 million Americans.
key_facts.excerpt: Alzheimer's disease agitation is the second neuropsychiatric indication for which Auvelity has received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation, and been granted FDA Priority Review and approval... a progressive and irreversible brain disorder, is the most common form of dementia, affecting more than 7 million Americans.

stories.headline: North Korea Stole $577M in Two Precision DeFi Hacks, Accounting for 76% of 2026 Crypto Losses

key_facts.fact: North Korean hackers stole approximately $577 million through the Drift Protocol ($285M, April 1) and KelpDAO ($292M, April 18) hacks, representing 76% of all crypto hack losses through April 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: North Korean hackers stole approximately USD 577 million in 2026 YTD — 76% of all crypto hack losses through April, across just a handful of attributed incidents.

key_facts.fact: The Drift Protocol attack involved months of unprecedented in-person social engineering, with North Korean proxies physically meeting Drift employees before draining funds in approximately 12 minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: The Drift Protocol attack was remarkable for its patience. On-chain staging began March 11, and the campaign involved in-person meetings between North Korean proxies and Drift employees over a period of months — a tactic TRM analysts described as potentially unprecedented.

key_facts.fact: The KelpDAO breach exploited a single-verifier design flaw in a LayerZero bridge; attackers compromised RPC nodes and launched a denial-of-service attack to drain ~116,500 rsETH (~$292M).
key_facts.excerpt: The attackers compromised two internal RPC nodes and then launched a denial-of-service attack against external nodes, forcing the bridge's single verifier to rely on the poisoned data sources... approximately 116,500 rsETH — worth roughly $292 million — was drained.

key_facts.fact: North Korea's share of total crypto hack losses has grown from under 10% in 2020-21 to 22% (2022), 37% (2023), 39% (2024), 64% (2025), and now 76% — the highest sustained share on record.
key_facts.excerpt: Pyongyang's share of total crypto hack losses has grown from under 10% in 2020 and 2021 to 22% in 2022, 37% in 2023, 39% in 2024, and 64% in 2025. The 2026 figure of 76% through April is the highest sustained share on record.

key_facts.fact: Cumulative North Korean crypto theft now exceeds $6 billion in attributed incidents since 2017, according to TRM Labs.
key_facts.excerpt: North Korea's cumulative crypto theft now exceeds $6 billion attributed incidents since 2017.

key_facts.fact: The KelpDAO theft triggered one of DeFi's largest wipeouts: $13 billion exited lending platforms in 48 hours, leaving Aave with a ~$200M bad-debt crisis now being backstopped by $300M in industry pledges.
key_facts.excerpt: After the attack, total value locked across Aave and DeFi as a whole fell sharply.
